methodology: Classical backbone = b1_2 source lexicon (Sarkar-attributed per varṇa) + operator primary-text corrections (ha, pa). v2 carried alongside for drift. This is a SEEDED framework for the careful per-varṇa classical update — NOT a finished re-derivation.
how_to_complete: For each varṇa with classical_review_status=LEXICON_ATTESTED_PENDING_PRIMARY_VERIFICATION, supply the primary classical text (as done for ha, pa), verify/adjust the poles, mark attested-vs-authored, and set review status to PRIMARY_TEXT_PROVIDED.
important_caveats: The LIBERATING pole is author counter-rewritten for most varṇas (lexicon rewrite_status) — not attested.
pa's operator reading PARTIALLY INVERTS the source-attested pole (ghṛṇā = the binding fetter). Recorded.

ha's binding/liberating SPLIT is researcher-authored over attested associations; motivated partly by making 'happy' cohere — MUST be frozen + pre-registered before any pole-test word/context authoring.
ṭha (ttha) classical night/moon reading vs lexicon 'Repentance' is unresolved — see classical_discrepancy.
Only 25 of 34 keys are bridge TARGETS; the 9 aspirates are reference-only.
Of those 25, FIVE (tta/dda/nna/nya/ssa) are fed only by cluster phonemes (tr/dr/nr/ny/shr) the English G2P never emits, so they are PRACTICALLY UNREACHABLE. Real English coverage is ~20 of 34 varṇas.

RETROFLEX UNDER-REPRESENTATION: English 'dr'/'tr' (drum, train) are phonetically retroflex-flavored — the bridge even maps dr->dda, tr->tta — but the G2P PRE-SPLITS the cluster into d+r / t+r, so those words map to DENTAL da/ta and the retroflex ḍa/ṭa are never produced. Capturing them needs a decomposer rule (d/t before r -> retroflex), which is a G2P change, not retrofitted here.
resonance_framing: RESONANCE refinement, not validated meaning. No ontology, no semantic truth, no Sanskrit privilege, no GENUTILITY_*, no ONTOLOGICAL_SIGNAL.
to_go_live_checklist: 1. Complete per-varṇa classical verification (fill PRIMARY_TEXT for the pending entries).
2. Operator sign-off (set status APPLIED); rename to varna_polarity_table_v3.json.
3. Re-point builders (pole-DiD / pole-sanity) to v3; re-derive packets; re-freeze declarations.
4. Pre-register the pole test BEFORE authoring any target words/contexts (anti-circularity).
5. Report results as RESONANCE legibility only — never validated meaning.

ba.source_note: Sarkar: acoustic root of avajñā vrtti (indifference / neglect of the valuable).
ba.worldly_binding_distortion: neglect of what actually has value
ba.spiritual_liberating_reading: regard that recognizes and attends to worth
ba.functional_operation: attends to and honors what has real value instead of neglecting it
ba.contrast_boundary: not goodwill against revulsion (Pa), not gladness at fortune (Ṇa)

bha.source_note: Sarkar: acoustic root of mūrcchā vrtti (loss of common sense under a ripu's hypnotic spell).
bha.worldly_binding_distortion: hypnotic entrancement, loss of common sense
bha.spiritual_liberating_reading: breaking the entrancing spell into clear sense
bha.functional_operation: snaps an externally-induced hypnotic fixation and restores clear common sense

ca.sanskrit_label: Viveka (conscience / discernment — real vs unreal, right vs wrong)
ca.english_rendering: Discernment (real vs unreal, right vs wrong)
ca.source_note: Sarkar: Ca is the acoustic root of viveka (conscience/discrimination); the discerning capacity is source-attested.
ca.source_quote_verified: Sarkar: 'Ca is the acoustic root of viveka [conscience].' — This is the ENTIRE classical passage: it attests ONLY the vṛtti name. No binding/liberating contrast and no further associations are given.
ca.worldly_binding_distortion: viveka distorted — discernment hardening into judgmentalism / separation-pride (discrimination used to feel superior to others)
ca.spiritual_liberating_reading: falsehood-discerning insight without egoic superiority — clear conscience distinguishing real from unreal, held without pride
ca.functional_operation: separates truth from falsehood by detecting misperception, distortion, and false appearance
ca.contrast_boundary: not Va/dharma, not assent, not acceptance-as-true, not conduct-ordering
ca.attested_vs_authored: PRIMARY-TEXT SCOPE = NAME ONLY. ATTESTED: ca = viveka (conscience/discernment), a LIBERATING-oriented faculty (its natural pole is the clear-conscience side; the binding pole is its DISTORTION, not its absence). AUTHORED (fully): BOTH pole texts are supplied by the source lexicon / framework — the one-line passage gives no binding/liberating contrast. Highest authored component so far; treat the poles as lexicon-supplied, not primary-verified.
ca.english_equivalent: the affricate /tʃ/ — the 'ch' sound (church, chair, match); bridge maps ch -> ca. BRIDGE-REACHABLE (church -> ca, ra, ca).
ca.v2_drift_note: v2 binding='lack of discrimination / confused discernment' sets the binding pole as the ABSENCE of viveka rather than its DISTORTION — a category error for a liberating-oriented faculty (binding = the faculty MISUSED, not missing). v3 (lexicon) uses 'discernment hardening into judgment / separation-pride.' v2 liberating ('conscience as inner dharmic compass') is acceptable. ca is bridge-reachable (ch-words: church/chair/match).

cha.source_note: Sarkar: acoustic root of vikalatā vrtti (nervous breakdown).
cha.source_quote_verified: Sarkar: Cha is the acoustic root of vikalatā vṛtti (nervous breakdown). A nervous breakdown occurs when one's mind, which had previously been functioning properly, either starts malfunctioning or stops functioning altogether. [Attests the vṛtti name + a definition of the state — no binding/liberating contrast is given; the poles below are lexicon/framework-supplied.]
cha.worldly_binding_distortion: collapse of mental function under strain — the mind that had functioned properly begins to malfunction or stops altogether
cha.spiritual_liberating_reading: steadiness that keeps mental function intact under load — holding the mind operational under a strain that would otherwise break it
cha.functional_operation: holds the mind operational under a load that would otherwise break it
cha.contrast_boundary: not threat-steadiness (Pha), not forbearance (Da), not poised rest (Ga)
cha.attested_vs_authored: PRIMARY-TEXT SCOPE = NAME + DEFINITION. ATTESTED: cha = vikalatā vṛtti (nervous breakdown), defined as a properly-functioning mind that starts malfunctioning or ceases — this MATCHES the binding pole. AUTHORED: the LIBERATING pole (steadiness that keeps function intact under load) is lexicon/framework-supplied; the passage defines the breakdown state but gives no liberating pole.
cha.english_equivalent: none — aspirated palatal (छ). English has no aspirated palatal; /tʃ/ ('ch') maps to ca (unaspirated). NOT bridge-reachable.
cha.v2_drift_note: cha is ABSENT from v2 (bridge-unreachable aspirate — reference-only). English has no aspirated palatal; /tʃ/ ('ch') maps to ca (unaspirated), so cha cannot arise in an English varṇa sequence.

da.source_note: Sarkar: acoustic root of peevishness (krodha / karkaśatā).
da.functional_operation: absorbs present provocation from another without discharging it back
da.contrast_boundary: not self-remorse-release (Ṭha), not shame-release (Ḍa), not poised rest (Ga)
da.attested_vs_authored: Attested side = classical_side below; the OTHER pole is largely author counter-rewritten (lexicon rewrite_status='source_preserved_counter_rewritten') — flagged, not validated.
da.v2_liberating: small egoic contraction; patience softens it

dda.source_note: Sarkar: acoustic root of lajjā vrtti (shyness).
dda.source_quote_verified: Sarkar: 'Ḍa is the acoustic root of lajjā vṛtti [the propensity of shyness].' — This is the ENTIRE classical passage: it attests only the vṛtti name.
dda.worldly_binding_distortion: lajjā as inhibition — action held back by others' regard; shrinking, self-conscious shame that blocks natural conduct
dda.spiritual_liberating_reading: acting unhindered by social shame — natural, unselfconscious conduct; healthy modesty without inhibition
dda.classical_associations: Cross-reference: lajjā is one of the eight pāshas (fetters) listed under pa (hatred, doubt, fear, shyness, dissemblance, vanity-of-lineage, cultural-superiority, egotism). (Not a pole.)
dda.functional_operation: releases the inhibiting grip of others' regard on action
dda.attested_vs_authored: PRIMARY-TEXT SCOPE = NAME ONLY. ATTESTED: dda = lajjā vṛtti (shyness); and (from the pa passage) lajjā is one of the eight pāshas/fetters. AUTHORED (fully): BOTH poles are lexicon-supplied — this one-line passage gives no binding/liberating contrast.
dda.english_equivalent: retroflex ḍa. A bridge TARGET exists (phoneme 'dr' -> dda) but the English G2P never emits 'dr' (splits d+r: drum -> da, ra), so dda is PRACTICALLY UNREACHABLE (retroflex series). PHONETIC NOTE: English 'dr' (drum/drive/dragon) IS retroflex-flavored — classically the d in 'drum' would be ḍa (THIS varṇa), and the bridge even encodes 'dr'->dda. But because the G2P pre-splits 'dr' into d+r, drum maps to da (DENTAL, krodha/irritability), ra, ma — so ḍa is never produced. Capturing it would need a decomposer rule treating d/t-before-r as retroflex ḍ/ṭ (a G2P change, NOT retrofitted here). This is an UNDER-representation of retroflexes, not just unreachability.
dda.v2_liberating: humility if purified; blockage if fear-based
dda.v2_drift_note: v2 binding='shyness' is the bare vṛtti NAME (not a distortion); v2 liberating='humility if purified; blockage if fear-based' is a hedged conditional, not a clean liberated MODE. v3 uses the lexicon's 'acting unhindered by social shame.' PRACTICALLY UNREACHABLE (retroflex; 'dr' never emitted).

ddha.sanskrit_label: Piśunatā (senseless / sadistic cruelty — torturous killing, malice)
ddha.source_note: Sarkar: acoustic root of piśunatā (senseless / sadistic cruelty).
ddha.source_quote_verified: Sarkar: Senseless, sadistic killing is called piśunatā vṛtti. Slaughtering in the way that inflicts the LEAST pain is NOT piśunatā; but killing slowly and cruelly — first chopping off legs, then tail, then head — is definitely piśunatā. (A live tortoise part-chopped and left crawling in its own blood; criminals impaled on spikes, half-buried and salted for dogs, or flayed alive — all examples of piśunatā.) The killing of animals, however done, is contrary to the spirit of Neohumanism.
ddha.worldly_binding_distortion: piśunatā — senseless, sadistic cruelty: harming/killing with gratuitous torture (dismembering a creature piece by piece; impaling, flaying), inflicting maximal suffering for its own sake; malice toward the maligned
ddha.spiritual_liberating_reading: compassion that shields the maligned — restraint from gratuitous cruelty; if life must be taken, with the minimum of pain (the spirit of Neohumanism)
ddha.classical_associations: Distinctions: piśunatā (sadistic torture) is NOT ordinary least-pain killing; it is a sharper/darker sibling of krūratā (la — cruelty / physical harm to the weak) and ENTIRELY DIFFERENT from dha (dental aspirate = tṛṣṇā / craving — operator-flagged 'different from Dha'). Held contrary to the spirit of Neohumanism.
ddha.functional_operation: turns malice-energy toward protecting the maligned (social harm)
ddha.contrast_boundary: not protection of the physically weak (La), not goodwill against revulsion (Pa)
ddha.attested_vs_authored: PRIMARY-TEXT SCOPE = NAME + rich DEFINITION/illustration. ATTESTED: ddha = piśunatā vṛtti (sadistic cruelty), vividly illustrated (torturous slaughter; the tortoise; impaling/flaying) — the BINDING pole; plus the attested contrast that least-pain killing is NOT piśunatā. AUTHORED: the LIBERATING pole (compassion shielding the maligned) is lexicon-supplied, though the passage's least-pain / Neohumanism contrast supports it.
ddha.english_equivalent: none — retroflex aspirate (ढ); doubly unreachable (retroflex AND aspirate), not a bridge target.
ddha.v2_drift_note: ddha is ABSENT from v2 (reference-only — retroflex AND aspirate, doubly unreachable). DISTINCT from dha (dental aspirate = tṛṣṇā / craving) — a different vṛtti entirely (operator note); and distinct from la (krūratā, general cruelty), of which piśunatā is the sadistic-torture intensification.

dha.source_note: Sarkar: acoustic root of thirst for acquisition (tṛṣṇā).
dha.spiritual_liberating_reading: the acquisitive thirst quenched at its root
dha.functional_operation: extinguishes the thirst-to-acquire itself, not merely one object
dha.contrast_boundary: not outcome-release (Ka), not object non-possession (Gha), not anti-hoarding (Jha)
dha.attested_vs_authored: Attested side = classical_side below; the OTHER pole is largely author counter-rewritten (lexicon rewrite_status='source_preserved_counter_rewritten') — flagged, not validated.
dha.v2_liberating: bondage through endless acquisition; spiritual ideation redirects it

ga.sanskrit_label: Ceṣṭā (effort / striving to arouse dormant potential)
ga.source_note: Sarkar: acoustic root of ceṣṭā vrtti (effort to arouse dormant potential).
ga.source_quote_verified: Sarkar: Every entity has the potentiality of expression; an animate entity can arouse that dormant potentiality through both internal and external means. If poetic genius lies dormant in someone and he arouses it by applying his will-force, he becomes a renowned poet; if lethargy prevents it, the genius stays unexpressed. The effort made to arouse one's dormant potentiality is called ceṣṭā. Ceṣṭā is one of the psychic vṛttis and is the MAIN CAUSE of mundane development AND spiritual elevation — its value in the mundane and supramundane spheres is immense. Ga, the acoustic root of ceṣṭā, plays an important role in the physical, psychic and spiritual spheres.
ga.worldly_binding_distortion: restless striving that cannot stop — effort compulsively driven on, unable to cease (and, clung to mundane ends, ceaseless outward striving)
ga.spiritual_liberating_reading: will-force applied to arouse one's dormant higher potential — purposeful effort that exerts and then rests into poised, alert repose without inertia; the effort behind spiritual elevation
ga.classical_associations: ceṣṭā = the effort to arouse dormant potentiality (latent genius -> applied will-force -> expression; else unexpressed). Described as the MAIN CAUSE of BOTH mundane development AND spiritual elevation, operating across the physical, psychic and spiritual spheres. (Scope/significance of the vṛtti — NOT a separate cosmological association.)
ga.functional_operation: exerts, then ceases into stable alert repose without inertia
ga.contrast_boundary: not dull inertia (Ta), not outcome-release (Ka), not containment (Ma)
ga.attested_vs_authored: ATTESTED: ga = ceṣṭā vṛtti (effort to arouse dormant potential); its immense value in BOTH the mundane and supramundane spheres. AUTHORED: the binding/liberating split (restless-can't-stop striving vs poised effort-that-rests / spiritually-elevating will-force) applies the framework's restlessness-vs-poise principle (consistent with the source lexicon); the passage frames ceṣṭā as valuable in both spheres and does not itself label a binding pole.
ga.v2_liberating: effort as path to mundane development and spiritual elevation
ga.v2_drift_note: v2 binding='effort / striving' is the bare vṛtti NAME, not a binding distortion; v2 liberating='effort as path to mundane development and spiritual elevation' paraphrases the passage's general VALUE statement about ceṣṭā (both spheres) rather than a distinct liberated mode — a mild value/association-into-pole conflation. v3 adopts the lexicon's crisper restless-vs-poised polarity.

gha.source_note: Sarkar: acoustic root of mamatā (love/attachment bound by time, space, individuality).
gha.source_quote_verified: Sarkar: Mamatā, the vṛtti of love and attachment, is related to time, space and individuality. People praise even the poorest goods made in their own country and criticize the best goods made elsewhere — irrational attachment for a place, a psychic disease (SPACE). A mother who sacrifices everything for her child mercilessly slices living kai fish without feeling, deaf to their agony (INDIVIDUALITY). The mother cow who lovingly licks her calf today kicks it away when it grows tomorrow (TIME). Thus mamatā is limited by the relative factors. Only human beings can make mamatā TRANSCEND the boundaries of time, space and individuality, after persistent and intense effort — impossible for other beings. Gha is the acoustic root of mamatā vṛtti.
gha.worldly_binding_distortion: mamatā bounded by the relative factors (time, space, individuality) — partial, possessive 'mine-ness' that clings to its own (own child, own country, own moment) while excluding or even harming what lies outside it
gha.spiritual_liberating_reading: mamatā made to TRANSCEND time, space and individuality — love expanded past its relative boundaries into universal affection that holds the loved on an open hand (achievable only by human beings, through persistent, intense effort)
gha.classical_associations: mamatā is related to time, space and individuality; its bounded form shows as place-attachment (praising one's own poor goods over better foreign ones — a 'psychic disease'), individuality (the mother who cherishes her child yet slices kai fish unmoved), and time (the cow that licks its calf today, kicks it away grown tomorrow). (Illustrations/scope of the vṛtti — not a separate cosmological association.)
gha.functional_operation: loves while relinquishing ownership of the object
gha.contrast_boundary: not outcome-release (Ka), not thirst-cessation (Dha), not indifference (Ba)
gha.attested_vs_authored: ATTESTED — and unusually so: gha = mamatā vṛtti (love/attachment); its limitation by time/space/individuality; and that only humans can make it TRANSCEND those boundaries through effort. The binding (bounded attachment) vs liberating (boundary-transcending universal love) split is directly SUPPORTED by the passage's own bounded-vs-transcendent contrast — lighter authored component than most entries.
gha.v2_drift_note: gha is ABSENT from v2 (bridge-unreachable aspirate — reference-only). English G2P has no /gh/ phoneme; written 'gh' yields /g/ -> ga (or is silent, e.g. 'rough'), so gha cannot arise in an English varṇa sequence.

ha.source_note: Sarkar: Ha = acoustic root of parā-vidyā (intuitional science). Knowledge binds unless realized.
ha.source_quote_verified: Sarkar: Ha = acoustic root of the ethereal (ākāśa) factor, of daytime, of the sun, of svarloka, and of parā-vidyā. Opposite to ha is ṭha, the acoustic root of nighttime, of the moon, of bhúvarloka, and of the kāmamaya kośa. Ha + ao = hao = acoustic root of Shiva in His táṇḍava posture.
ha.worldly_binding_distortion: outward / visible vision — fixation on the manifest, physically-seen, outward-facing world
ha.classical_associations: ether (ākāśa) factor; daytime; sun; svarloka; parā-vidyā. OPPOSITE varṇa = ṭha (night, moon, bhúvarloka, kāmamaya kośa). COMPOUND ha+ao = hao = Shiva's táṇḍava. (Associations + an opposite varṇa — NOT an intra-ha polarity.)
ha.functional_operation: lets knowledge dissolve identity instead of forming spiritual ego
ha.contrast_boundary: not information, not doctrine, not intellectual certainty
ha.attested_vs_authored: ATTESTED: the associations above. AUTHORED: the binding/liberating SPLIT (outward-visible vs inner-intuitional) is researcher-imposed; motivated partly by making 'happy' cohere — freeze + pre-register before word/context authoring.
ha.v2_binding: night / darkness (the contractive opposite of ha = day / sun / light)
ha.v2_liberating: svarloka, solar ascent, Shivaic dynamism, tandava force
ha.v2_drift_note: v2 binding='night/darkness' imported the OPPOSITE varṇa ṭha's domain into ha's cell (category error); v2 also folded the COMPOUND hao's táṇḍava into bare ha.

ja.source_note: Sarkar: acoustic root of ahaṁkāra vrtti (ego / inflated I-feeling).
ja.source_quote_verified: Sarkar: Ja is the acoustic root of ahaṃkāra vṛtti (ego). The ego becomes inflated when one allows one's 'I' feeling to take a predominant role. 'Since I was there, I was able to control the situation... had I not been there the world would have met its final destruction.' — so spoke Aurangzeb; it is an expression of ahaṃkāra vṛtti. [Attests the vṛtti name + an illustration of the INFLATED (binding) form; no liberating pole is given.]
ja.worldly_binding_distortion: the inflated 'I did / I control this' — the 'I'-feeling swollen into sole doership (as in Aurangzeb: 'had I not been there the world would have been destroyed')
ja.spiritual_liberating_reading: agency exercised WITHOUT inflating the 'I' — acting and functioning while not claiming sole doership
ja.functional_operation: acts while withdrawing the inflated I-claim from the account of events
ja.contrast_boundary: not outward display-dropping (Ṅa), not inner/outer honesty (Ña)
ja.attested_vs_authored: PRIMARY-TEXT SCOPE = NAME + ILLUSTRATION. ATTESTED: ja = ahaṃkāra vṛtti (ego), with the Aurangzeb illustration of the inflated 'I' — matching the BINDING pole. AUTHORED: the LIBERATING pole (agency without inflating the I) is lexicon-supplied; the passage illustrates only the inflated (binding) form.
ja.english_equivalent: the affricate /dʒ/ — the 'j' sound (judge, jam, joy); G2P emits the 'jh' phoneme -> bridge maps jh -> ja. BRIDGE-REACHABLE (judge -> ja, da, ga; joy -> ja).
ja.v2_drift_note: v2 binding='ego / inflated I-feeling' is fine; but v2 liberating='identity bondage; false doership' RESTATES the ego PROBLEM rather than a liberated mode — the same problem-as-pole error seen at nga and elsewhere. v3 uses the lexicon's 'agency exercised without inflating the I.' ja is bridge-reachable (j-words: judge/jam/joy).

jha.source_note: Sarkar: acoustic root of lolupatā, lobha (greed) and lolatā (avarice).
jha.source_quote_verified: Sarkar: Jha is the acoustic root of lolupatā, lobha (greed) and lolatā (avarice) vṛttis. The Bengali word nolā (the greedy fascination of a cat or a dog) is derived from lola / lolatā.
jha.worldly_binding_distortion: greed / avarice — hoarding accumulation without limit; the insatiable greedy fascination (nolā) that always wants more
jha.spiritual_liberating_reading: sufficiency — appetite that releases at 'enough'; wanting stilled at contentment, the surplus grip let go
jha.classical_associations: Etymology: the Bengali nolā (a cat's or dog's greedy fascination) derives from lola / lolatā. (An etymological illustration of the vṛtti — not a separate association or pole.)
jha.functional_operation: stops accumulation at sufficiency and releases the surplus grip
jha.contrast_boundary: not thirst-cessation (Dha), not non-possessive love (Gha), not outcome-release (Ka)
jha.attested_vs_authored: PRIMARY-TEXT SCOPE = NAME + ETYMOLOGY. ATTESTED: jha = lolupatā/lobha/lolatā vṛttis (greed/avarice), illustrated by nolā. AUTHORED: the binding/liberating split (limitless hoarding vs sufficiency-that-releases) is lexicon/framework-supplied; the passage names the vṛtti and its etymology but gives no pole contrast.
jha.english_equivalent: none — aspirated palatal affricate (झ). English /dʒ/ emits the 'jh' phoneme, but the bridge maps 'jh' -> ja (unaspirated), so the aspirate jha is NOT bridge-reachable.
jha.v2_drift_note: jha is ABSENT from v2 (bridge-unreachable aspirate — reference-only). English /dʒ/ emits phoneme 'jh' but the bridge maps 'jh' -> ja (unaspirated), so the aspirate jha cannot arise in an English varṇa sequence.

ka.source_note: Sarkar: Ka is the acoustic root of the abhīpsātmaka āśā vrtti (hope).
ka.source_quote_verified: Sarkar: Ka = acoustic root of the abhiipśātmaka āśā vṛtti (the propensity of hope), which goads creatures — especially humans — to work in various ways. Ka is ALSO the acoustic root of Kārya Brahma (the expressed universe). Etymology: ka (kae + ḍa) = 'that which produces sound'; also 'water' (flowing water; va = water in general); also 'hair grown on the head' (kac = glossy). Ka + iisha = kesha (hair; also Nārāyaṇa). Kārya Brahma (Saguṇarasātmaka Brahma), represented by ka, is the controller of the living world; Buddhist Saṃvṛtti Bodhicitta = the created world = Kārya Brahma (kāpālika: 'Kaṃ saṃvṛtti bodhicittaṃ pālayati').
ka.worldly_binding_distortion: āśā as grasping / clinging hope — goaded toward a specific outcome or object; the downward pull of attached desire
ka.spiritual_liberating_reading: aspiring hope held WITHOUT attachment — forward-orientation that acts while releasing the grip on the result (oriented toward the Great, not the object)
ka.classical_associations: ka = Kārya Brahma (the expressed / created universe; Saguṇarasātmaka Brahma; controller of the living world); 'that which produces sound'; 'water' / flowing water (va = water in general); 'hair on the head' (kesha = ka+iisha, also a name of Nārāyaṇa); Buddhist Saṃvṛtti Bodhicitta. These are cosmological / etymological ASSOCIATIONS of ka, NOT poles.
ka.functional_operation: aspires and acts while releasing the grip on the result
ka.contrast_boundary: not object-renunciation (Gha), not craving-cessation (Dha), not de-fascination (Na)
ka.attested_vs_authored: ATTESTED: ka = āśā vṛtti (hope that goads action) AND ka = Kārya Brahma (expressed universe) + sound/water/hair associations. AUTHORED: the binding/liberating SPLIT of hope (grasping vs non-attached) applies the general attachment principle — the source states āśā goads action but does not itself split it into poles.
ka.v2_liberating: expressed universe, creation-field, emergence into manifestation
ka.v2_drift_note: v2 put the Kārya-Brahma ASSOCIATION ('expressed universe, creation-field, emergence into manifestation') into the LIBERATING POLE — conflating an attested cosmological association with the liberated form of hope (a category error). The liberating pole of āśā is non-attached aspiration, not 'the created universe.'

kha.source_note: Sarkar: acoustic root of cintā vrtti (worry / impersonal, objective thought).
kha.source_quote_verified: Sarkar: The acoustic root of āśā vṛtti is ka; that of cintā vṛtti (the propensity of worry) is kha. If your train runs late you think not only of the delay but of the probable inconveniences (the host, arriving late for food, deciding to eat near the station) — such consequential thoughts are symbolized by kha. Travelling elsewhere you might reflect on a collapsing brassware industry and whether it could be revived, though you are 'not personally affected' and 'not a direct player in your own thoughts' — such impersonal thoughts are also kha. Kha MEANS 'sky' but is NOT the acoustic root of the sky (that is ha); kha also means 'heaven', but only its CRUDE aspects — the sphere of heaven that transcends the crude is kṣa. Ka = Kārya Brahma is the first consonant; and since ka + ha = kha, kha immediately follows ka in the Indo-Aryan alphabet.
kha.worldly_binding_distortion: cintā as anxious rumination — the mind churning over unresolved contingencies and personal consequences (e.g. worrying through the late-train inconveniences), gripping the what-ifs
kha.spiritual_liberating_reading: cintā as composed, impersonal reflection — holding an unsettled situation open without forcing premature closure; objective contemplation in which one is 'not a direct player' (e.g. weighing how a failing industry might be revived), reflection without anxious grip
kha.classical_associations: Paired with ka: ka = āśā (hope) goads action; kha = cintā (worry / objective thought) reflects. kha MEANS 'sky' and 'heaven' but is NOT their acoustic root — the SKY's root is ha; kha = the CRUDE aspects of heaven, while the transcendent sphere = kṣa (ksha). Structurally ka + ha = kha (hence kha follows ka, the first consonant / Kārya Brahma, in the alphabet). These are meanings/associations, NOT poles.
kha.functional_operation: holds an unsettled impersonal situation open without forcing premature closure
kha.contrast_boundary: not self-efficacy (Ya), not threat-steadiness (Pha), not firmness-under-strain (Cha)
kha.attested_vs_authored: ATTESTED: kha = cintā vṛtti; the personal (train) vs impersonal (industry) modes; kha ≠ the sky's root (ha is), kha = crude heaven vs kṣa = transcendent heaven; ka + ha = kha. AUTHORED: labelling anxious/gripping rumination as binding and composed impersonal openness as liberating applies the framework's fixation-vs-detachment principle (consistent with the source lexicon); the passage describes both modes as cintā without itself labelling them binding/liberating.
kha.v2_drift_note: kha is ABSENT from v2 (bridge-unreachable aspirate — reference-only). English G2P renders written 'kh' as ka + ha (two SEPARATE roots = hope + vision), which does NOT reconstruct cintā — a semantic mismatch, even though ka + ha = kha holds structurally in the classical alphabet.

nga.source_note: Sarkar: acoustic root of dambha vrtti (vanity).
nga.source_quote_verified: Sarkar: Uṋa (ṅa) is the acoustic root of dambha vṛtti (vanity). The popular story: the sage Vashiṣṭha travelled to China to learn the Chinese school of Tantra, learned the use of una in Tantric mantras, and introduced it in India; una is used extensively across the Indo-Chinese languages (Tibetan, Ladakhi, Sherpa, Manpa). Its transmission is linked to the Tárā cult, trifurcated as Ugra/Vajra Tárā (India), Nīla Tárā / Nīla Sarasvatī (Tibet), and Bhrāmarī / Kṛṣṇa Tárā (China). The acoustic root of Vajra Tárā and Nīla Tárā is aeṃ; that of the black Bhrāmarī Tárā (= Kālī in Varṇāśrama Dharma) is krīṃ (ka = Kārya Brahma + ra = the luminous factor).
nga.worldly_binding_distortion: dambha as vanity — the self displayed and performed for others' eyes; conduct staged to be seen and admired
nga.spiritual_liberating_reading: conduct that stands without outward performance — action done for its own sake, needing no audience or applause
nga.classical_associations: Phonetic-historical (NOT poles): per the legend, una was learned by Vashiṣṭha in China and introduced to India, and is used across the Indo-Chinese languages (Tibetan/Ladakhi/Sherpa/Manpa). Its transmission is tied to the Tárā cult — but the Tárā deities have their OWN acoustic roots (aeṃ for Vajra/Nīla Tárā; krīṃ = ka[Kārya Brahma] + ra[luminous factor] for Bhrāmarī Tárā / Kālī), NOT una. Record as history/association; do not fold aeṃ/krīṃ/Tárā into nga's poles.
nga.functional_operation: acts without staging the self for approval
nga.contrast_boundary: not inner I-claim deflation (Ja), not inner/outer honesty (Ña)
nga.attested_vs_authored: ATTESTED: nga (uṋa/ṅa) = dambha vṛtti (vanity); the phonetic history (Chinese-origin legend, Indo-Chinese usage) and the Tárā-cult context with the deities' SEPARATE roots aeṃ/krīṃ. AUTHORED: the binding/liberating split (displayed-for-others vs conduct-without-performance) applies the framework's display-vs-unselfconscious principle (consistent with the source lexicon); the passage states the vṛtti but does not itself split it into poles.
nga.english_equivalent: the velar nasal /ŋ/ — the 'ng' sound (sing, king, long, song); bridge maps the /ŋ/ phoneme -> nga. BRIDGE-REACHABLE (e.g. longing -> la, nga, nga; king -> ka, nga).
nga.v2_liberating: egoic obstruction; humility is its spiritual correction
nga.v2_drift_note: v2 binding='vanity / pride-display' is close to attested, but v2 liberating='egoic obstruction; humility is its spiritual correction' restates the vṛtti's PROBLEM and names its corrective (humility) rather than giving the liberated MODE of conduct. v3 adopts the lexicon's crisper 'conduct that stands without outward performance.' (nga is bridge-reachable — this revises packets for ng-words such as longing/king/song.)

nya.source_note: Sarkar: acoustic root of kapaṭatā vrtti (hypocrisy).
nya.source_quote_verified: Sarkar: Iṋa (ña) is the acoustic root of kapaṭatā vṛtti (hypocrisy). Another Sanskrit word for hypocrite is páśaṇḍa; in Hindi, pākhaṇḍī. Hypocrisy takes many forms; three common ones: (1) getting one's purpose served by exploiting or cheating others; (2) unnecessarily dominating somebody to conceal one's own ignorance or weakness; (3) pretending to be moral by criticizing the sins of others which one secretly commits oneself.
nya.worldly_binding_distortion: hypocrisy / concealment — inner and outer diverging: cheating to serve one's purpose, domineering to hide one's own weakness, condemning in others the sins one secretly commits
nya.spiritual_liberating_reading: transparency — inner intent and outer act coincide; no pretense, being what one appears
nya.classical_associations: Sanskrit páśaṇḍa / Hindi pākhaṇḍī = hypocrite. Three illustrated forms of hypocrisy (all of the BINDING pole): exploit/cheat to serve one's purpose; dominate to conceal one's ignorance/weakness; feign morality by condemning others' secretly-shared sins.
nya.functional_operation: aligns inner intent with outer act, removing concealment
nya.attested_vs_authored: PRIMARY-TEXT SCOPE = NAME + FORMS. ATTESTED: nya = kapaṭatā vṛtti (hypocrisy), with three illustrated forms — all of the BINDING pole. AUTHORED: the LIBERATING pole (transparency, inner=outer) is lexicon-supplied; the passage illustrates only the hypocritical (binding) form.
nya.english_equivalent: the palatal nasal /ɲ/ (ña). A bridge TARGET exists (phoneme 'ny' -> nya), BUT the English G2P NEVER emits 'ny' (canyon -> ...na, ya...; lasagna/señor/vignette -> g+n or plain n), so nya is PRACTICALLY UNREACHABLE — effectively reference-only for English despite being one of v2's 25 keys.
nya.v2_liberating: spiritual falseness; split between outer virtue and inner conduct
nya.v2_drift_note: v2 binding='hypocrisy / deceit' is fine; v2 liberating='spiritual falseness; split between outer virtue and inner conduct' RESTATES the hypocrisy PROBLEM (the split) as the liberating pole — the same problem-as-pole error as nga/ja. v3 uses the lexicon's 'transparency — inner intent and outer act coincide.' Also PRACTICALLY UNREACHABLE in English (G2P never emits 'ny').

pa.source_note: Sarkar: acoustic root of ghṛṇā vrtti (hatred / revulsion).
pa.source_quote_verified: Sarkar: Pa = acoustic root of ghṛṇā vṛtti (hatred/revulsion), the FETTER of hatred (one of the eight pāshas), stemming mainly from moha. 'When one's psychic attraction is toward the crude, the mind has a downward tendency (pat/patati) leading to downfall; when the mind moves upward it is anurakti (attraction for the Great), whose consummation is devotion.'
pa.worldly_binding_distortion: attraction toward the crude / objects — the downward-pulling pull (pat / patati -> downfall)
pa.spiritual_liberating_reading: revulsion OF the ripus — ghṛṇā redirected against the crude/vices (vairāgya-like turning)
pa.classical_associations: ghṛṇā = the fetter of hatred (one of the eight pāshas: hatred, doubt, fear, shyness, dissemblance, vanity-of-lineage, cultural-superiority, egotism); six ripus = kāma, krodha, lobha, mada, moha, mātsarya; downward attraction (pat) vs upward anurakti -> devotion.
pa.functional_operation: converts revulsion toward another into active goodwill
pa.contrast_boundary: not compassion for the suffering (Ḍha/La), not gladness at fortune (Ṇa)
pa.attested_vs_authored: ATTESTED: pa = ghṛṇā (revulsion), classically a binding FETTER; the downward-attraction vs upward-anurakti contrast. AUTHORED/REINTERPRETED: making revulsion the LIBERATING pole and attraction the BINDING pole PARTIALLY INVERTS the attested assignment (ghṛṇā/hatred is classically the binding fetter).
pa.v2_liberating: fetter of hatred; related to moha and fear
pa.v2_drift_note: v2 and the source lexicon both place revulsion on the binding side; this operator reading inverts it.

tta.source_note: Sarkar: acoustic root of vitarka vrtti (overstating one's case).
tta.source_quote_verified: Sarkar: Ṭa is the acoustic root of vitarka vṛtti (overstating one's case). Vitarka is not merely debating; it means overstating one's case to the point of garrulousness — a combination of bad temper and garrulousness. It is NOT synonymous with kaśāya vṛtti (speaking harshly to hurt others). Example (Howrah station): asked whether the Uluberia local has left, one gentleman snaps abusively ('Am I a railway timetable?... People like you make life hell...') — uncontrolled vitarka; a second replies helpfully with just the relevant facts (platform eleven, five minutes) — pramita vāk (balanced statement, only relevant words).
tta.worldly_binding_distortion: vitarka — overstating one's case to the point of garrulousness; bad-tempered, exaggerated over-talk beyond what is warranted (the abusive over-response)
tta.spiritual_liberating_reading: pramita vāk — balanced, measured speech using only relevant words; saying just what is warranted (the helpful, to-the-point reply)
tta.classical_associations: Vitarka = bad temper + garrulousness; explicitly NOT kaśāya vṛtti (speaking harshly to hurt others). Its liberated contrast term is pramita vāk (balanced statement). (Distinctions/illustration, not a separate cosmological association.)
tta.functional_operation: trims expression to exactly the warranted amount
tta.contrast_boundary: not honesty of intent (Ña), not containment (Ma), not poised rest (Ga)
tta.attested_vs_authored: ATTESTED — BOTH poles: the passage explicitly contrasts uncontrolled vitarka (garrulous, bad-tempered overstatement — the abusive gentleman) with pramita vāk (balanced speech, only relevant words — the helpful gentleman), and distinguishes vitarka from kaśāya. Light authored component (the pole split is in the source).
tta.english_equivalent: retroflex ṭa. A bridge TARGET exists (phoneme 'tr' -> tta) but the English G2P never emits 'tr' (it splits t+r: train -> ta, ra, na), so tta is PRACTICALLY UNREACHABLE. PHONETIC NOTE (same as ḍa/dr): English 'tr' (train/tree/truck) is retroflex-flavored — classically the t would be ṭa (THIS varṇa), and the bridge encodes 'tr'->tta, but the G2P pre-splits 'tr' into t+r so train maps to ta (DENTAL), ra, na and ṭa is never produced. Under-representation of retroflexes; capturing it needs a decomposer rule for d/t-before-r.
tta.v2_liberating: misuse of speech; needs silence / balanced speech
tta.v2_drift_note: v2 binding='overstatement / garrulousness' is fine; v2 liberating='misuse of speech; needs silence / balanced speech' restates the PROBLEM ('misuse of speech') and names a corrective ('needs silence') rather than the liberated MODE. v3 uses the attested 'pramita vāk — measured speech saying only what is warranted.' PRACTICALLY UNREACHABLE: tta's source phoneme 'tr' is never emitted by the G2P (retroflex series).

ttha.source_note: Sarkar: acoustic root of anutāpa vrtti (repentance).
ttha.source_quote_verified: Sarkar: Ṭha is the acoustic root of anutāpa vṛtti (repentance). One is seized by repentance on realizing (from within, or with a second person's help) the impropriety of one's action. In northern India anutāpa is called paścāttāpa. Anu and paschāt both mean 'later / after'; tāpa means 'heat' (so repentance = 'after-heat').
ttha.worldly_binding_distortion: anutāpa as gripping remorse — the 'after-heat' that torments, replaying one's own past wrong without release
ttha.spiritual_liberating_reading: repentance discharged into acceptance — the remorse over one's past act released, the realization-of-impropriety turned into amendment rather than endless self-torment
ttha.classical_associations: COSMOLOGICAL (from the ha passage): ṭha is the acoustic root of nighttime, the moon, bhúvarloka, and the kāmamaya kośa — the contractive OPPOSITE of ha (day/sun/svarloka/parā-vidyā). ETYMOLOGY: anutāpa = anu ('after') + tāpa ('heat'); N. Indian paścāttāpa = paschāt ('after') + tāpa ('heat') = 'after-heat'. This RESOLVES the earlier ttha discrepancy: night/moon are ṭha's ASSOCIATIONS; its VṚTTI is anutāpa (repentance) — associations vs pole, as with ha/ka.
ttha.functional_operation: discharges remorse over one's own past act into acceptance
ttha.attested_vs_authored: ATTESTED: ṭha = anutāpa vṛtti (repentance); its definition (remorse on realizing impropriety); the anutāpa/paścāttāpa='after-heat' etymology; and (from the ha passage) its cosmological associations night/moon/bhúvarloka/kāmamaya kośa as ha's opposite. AUTHORED: the binding/liberating split (gripping remorse vs remorse-released-into-acceptance) is lexicon-supplied; this passage defines the state, not a pole contrast.
ttha.english_equivalent: none — retroflex aspirate (ठ); doubly unreachable (aspirate AND retroflex), not a bridge target.
ttha.v2_drift_note: ttha is ABSENT from v2 (reference-only — retroflex AND aspirate, doubly unreachable). RESOLVES the earlier v3 'ttha discrepancy': the ha passage's night/moon are ṭha's ASSOCIATIONS (its cosmological opposite-of-ha domain), while its VṚTTI is anutāpa (repentance). Corollary: v2's ha binding='night' was doubly wrong — night belongs to ṭha, and even for ṭha it is an association, not the pole.
ttha.classical_discrepancy: RESOLVED (see ledger): the ha passage associates ṭha (ttha) with nighttime/moon/bhúvarloka/kāmamaya kośa — the cosmological OPPOSITE of ha; its VṚTTI is anutāpa (repentance). Night/moon are ṭha's ASSOCIATIONS; anutāpa is its pole axis — associations vs pole, not a contradiction. (v2's ha binding='night' was doubly wrong: night is ṭha's, and even there an association, not a pole.)
